title: Purpuric rash: HSP or sepsis?
stem: Paediatric area. Miss Ramesh has brought her son Arjun, 6, who has developed a rash on his legs over a day. Take a history from her, and answer her questions.
notes:
Checked against NICE CG102 (meningococcal disease), NICE NG143 (Fever in under 5s) principles, and the EULAR/PRINTO/PRES criteria for IgA vasculitis (Henoch–Schönlein purpura).

A non-blanching rash in a febrile or unwell child is meningococcal disease until proven otherwise: antibiotics immediately. In a well child without fever, consider IgA vasculitis (HSP: palpable purpura on the buttocks and extensor legs, arthralgia/arthritis, abdominal pain, haematuria/proteinuria; often after an URTI), ITP (bruising and petechiae, isolated low platelets, well child), leukaemia (pallor, bone pain, lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly), trauma/NAI, and petechiae above the nipple line after coughing or vomiting.

Investigations: FBC and film, clotting, CRP, U&E, blood pressure, urinalysis (blood and protein), and blood cultures if febrile. HSP is managed supportively (analgesia); follow up with BP and urine checks for 6–12 months for nephritis; refer with abdominal pain (intussusception), significant proteinuria, hypertension or renal impairment.

Your notes (a well 6-year-old with a leg rash, knee ache, recent cold, no fever) match this.

Systemic.r: Some tummy ache yesterday. Urine looks normal.

Systemic.t: Nosebleeds, bleeding gums, bruising, tiredness, weight loss?

Background.r: Me, his dad and his sister. No injuries.

steps.label: Her questions
steps.hint: Explain likely HSP, the need to examine and test, and when to worry.

turns.line: I read that a rash that doesn't fade means meningitis. Is it that?

opts.t: You were right to bring him. Because he has no fever and is playing normally, this looks more like Henoch–Schönlein purpura — a harmless-looking inflammation of small blood vessels after a virus. I'll examine him fully and check his blood, blood pressure and urine to be sure.
opts.mark: Explains the likely diagnosis and need to examine and test

opts.r: How can you know without looking?

opts.t: Sometimes it affects the kidneys, usually mildly, so we check his urine and blood pressure now and regularly for about 6 months. Come back straight away if he gets severe tummy pain, blood in his poo, dark urine, swelling or a fever.

qs.q: Febrile child with a non-blanching rash: action?
wrong: Wait for the FBC, CRP and blood culture results

qs.a: Buttocks and extensor surfaces of the legs

qs.q: Why follow up urine and BP after HSP?
wrong: To detect a urinary tract infection
To monitor for hypertension from steroids

badge.name: Glass Half Clear
badge.flavor: Unwell or febrile: antibiotics. Well with leg purpura: think HSP, check urine.
